nodes.title: Choose Your References
widgets_values:
**Setup:** Load your source video, add the first 1–5 reference pictures, and choose Reference Count. Later pictures stay inactive and may be empty.

**Track:** Name the subjects already in the video, separated by commas. Set Max Objects. Blank Track IDs selects all detections; use 0,1,... to choose from the colored preview.

**Prompt:** Name each active Picture and explain what it replaces. The included text is a generic starting template.

**Full Scene:** OFF uses tracked masks; ON edits the entire scene and skips tracking.

**Timing:** frame_count = 0 uses the source timeline range. Keep 24 fps. Padding and final trimming are automatic. When changing a file, reload the timeline media and fit its range to the material.

nodes.title: Edit Prompt | Name each active Picture
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman's facial identity and blonde bob from <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> is the cheeseburger from <Picture 2>.
<Subject 3> is the cream floral dress from <Picture 3>. Both views show one garment.
<Video 1> is the source video being edited.

summary: [video editing + audio reuse]
The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace the woman's face and hair with <Subject 1>, the apple with <Subject 2>, and her tank top, pants, and belt with <Subject 3>. Each replacement is complete when its target first appears.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - apply the reference facial identity and blonde bob while following the woman's original expressions, gaze, and head movements.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the sesame bun, beef, melted cheese, lettuce, tomato, and onion, sized naturally for her hand.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the cream fabric, pink floral pattern, puff sleeves, sweetheart neckline, front tie, fitted waist, and short flared skirt with ruffled hem. Replace the original top, pants, and belt with this single dress.
<Video 1>: weak_reference - follow the original timing, poses, interactions, framing, and camera movement. Preserve the original griffin, stone wall, coastal setting, and the woman's boots.

detailed_description:
Photorealistic warm coastal daylight. [Shot 1] The blonde woman wears the floral dress and sits on the stone wall holding the cheeseburger. The original griffin stands beside her, spreads its feathered wings, and hops onto her shoulder. She bites the burger, then offers it to the griffin, following the source action.

The dress drapes naturally over her lap and upper thighs. Maintain believable hand and mouth contact, matching lighting and shadows, and consistent facial identity, hairstyle, burger appearance, and dress design. Follow each target's original visibility and keep its replacement consistent whenever it appears.

overall_soundscape:
Keep the original source soundtrack synchronized with the action.

non_diegetic_music:
Retain any music already present in the source soundtrack.

nodes.title: Prompting Guide | Reference Video Editing
widgets_values:
# Reference Video Editing: Prompting Guide

Build a complete description of the finished video. Use the four sections below and keep reference labels consistent throughout.

## 1. subject_definitions
Assign each replacement a `<Subject N>` label and bind it to the correct `<Picture N>`. Define `<Video 1>` as the source clip. Specify whether a reference supplies a whole design or selected features.

## 2. summary
State the edit: what each subject replaces and where it appears. For an immediate replacement, make it complete in the opening frame and consistent through the final frame.

## 3. retention_analysis
Explain what to take from each picture and what to preserve from the source video. Name defining shapes, colors, materials, facial features, clothing, or anatomy.

- **attribute_transfer:** transfer selected features.
- **fully_preserved:** retain the defined reference subject closely.
- **partially_preserved:** retain specified aspects while changing others.
- **weak_reference:** use broad reference guidance.

Follow each marker with ` - ` and a clear explanation. These describe intent; they are not numerical strength controls.

## 4. detailed_description
Describe style and lighting, then `[Shot 1]` and the opening composition. Explain actions in playback order, including grip, contact, occlusion, scale, perspective, and camera movement. End with the closing action and appearance. Use additional shots only for actual cuts.


## Before generating
- Match Picture numbers to the loaded reference order.
- State the exact replacement scope and source details to preserve.
- Describe the desired result with concrete visual details.
- Keep appearances consistent from the first frame to the last.
- Track the original subjects; describe replacements in the edit prompt.
- Check that masks cover the intended edits throughout the clip.

**Use the template beside this note.** Replace every brace-delimited placeholder. Repeat subject entries for additional references. Write enough detail to cover the edit; there is no fixed word count.

nodes.title: Prompt Template | Copy and Adapt
widgets_values:
# Reusable Prompt Template

Fill every `{placeholder}`. Add or remove subjects to match your references, and choose retention markers for the intended edit.

```text
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the {replacement subject or selected identity features} shown in <Picture 1>.
<Subject 2> is the {replacement object or character} shown in <Picture 2>.
<Video 1> is the source footage to be edited.

summary: [video editing + audio reuse]
The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace {original subject or selected region} with <Subject 1>, and {original second subject} with <Subject 2>. Both replacements are complete in the opening frame and remain consistent through the final frame.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - transfer {specific reference features} from <Picture 1> to {the intended subject or region}. Preserve {source features outside this edit}.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the complete reference design from <Picture 2>, including {shape, color, materials, proportions, and distinctive details}. Adapt its scale and orientation to {its placement or interaction} in the source.
<Video 1>: weak_reference - use {action timing, poses, contact, movement paths, and camera motion} as guidance. Retain {specific setting, lighting, clothing, or other source details}. Replaced appearances come from their assigned pictures.

detailed_description:
{Visual style, setting, and lighting}. [Shot 1] The opening frame shows <Subject 1> {position, pose, and appearance} and <Subject 2> {position and appearance}. Both already have their intended reference features before the action begins. {Describe the first action}. {Describe the next action, including relevant grip, contact, or occlusion}. {Describe the final action and closing composition}. Match perspective, scale, lighting, and contact shadows to the scene. Follow {source camera movement and framing}. Preserve {source timing and other relevant details}. Keep the {transferred features} of <Subject 1> and the complete reference design of <Subject 2> consistent from the first frame through the final frame.

overall_soundscape:
Keep the original source soundtrack, including {relevant ambience, dialogue, and action sounds}.

```

**Adapt the structure to the edit:** use `fully_preserved` for a complete design replacement, or `attribute_transfer` for selected features. Describe a gradual transformation only when it is intended. Adjust the audio sections if the task changes the soundtrack.
